info.description: Backend for the Birga caregiver app.
info.title: Birga API

get.description: Checks that the database is reachable.

post.description:
- title/description are required in both Uzbek (uz) and Russian (ru)
- goal is one of: language, motor, cognitive, social, emotional
- min_age/max_age are child ages in years, within 2..6

delete.description:
Sets deleted_at; the activity disappears from every list, get and recommendation.
Completions that point at it are kept.

patch.description:
- only the fields present in the body change; omitted or null fields are kept
- same rules as create; texts cannot be emptied; the resulting age range must stay valid (422)
- send {"is_published": true} to publish, false to hide it from the app
patch.summary: updates an activity partially, including publishing or unpublishing it

post.description:
- phone_number is required, in E.164 format (+998901234567)
- username is optional: 3..32 latin letters, digits, '_' or '.'; stored lowercase
- name is optional, at most 100 characters; photo_id is an optional id from POST /v1/media (422 if unknown)
- username and phone_number must be unique among non-deleted users (409)

delete.description:
Sets deleted_at; the user disappears from reads, their tokens are removed,
and their username and phone number can be used again.

patch.description:
- only the fields present in the body change; omitted or null fields are kept
- "" clears name, username or photo_id; phone_number cannot be cleared
- same format and uniqueness rules as create

post.description:
- first POST /v1/otp/send and /v1/otp/verify with purpose reset_password for the
user's phone number; without that verification: 403. A successful reset uses it up
- phone_number: +998 and 9 digits; password: 8 to 72 bytes, stored as a bcrypt hash (422)
- no user has this phone number: 404
- returns a new token pair (the user is signed in); every token issued before stops working
post.summary: sets a new password for a signed-out user, confirmed by an SMS code

post.description:
- username is case-insensitive; username and password are required (422)
- unknown username or wrong password: 401 with the same message, so it does not tell
which usernames exist
- returns a new token pair, like sign-up. Only the newest pair is valid, so signing in
signs out every other device
post.summary: signs a user in with username and password

post.description:
- the access token used here and the refresh token stop working at once (401 afterwards);
sign in again with POST /v1/auth/login

- refresh_token must be signed by this API, unexpired, of type refresh, and still the
one stored for the user (a deleted user's token stops working); otherwise 401
- the refresh token is not rotated; keep using it until it expires
post.summary: trades a refresh token for a new access token

post.description:
- no OTP step: the phone number is not verified, so every new user gets the role
unverified_user (stored in user_auth.role and written into the tokens as the role claim)
- name: 1 to 100 characters; username: 3 to 32 of a-z, 0-9, '_' or '.' (lowercased);
password: 8 to 72 bytes, stored as a bcrypt hash; phone_number: +998 and 9 digits (422)
- no profile photo here: set photo_id later with PATCH /v1/me
- username or phone number already used: 409
- access_token (JWT_ACCESS_TTL, default 24 hours) and refresh_token (JWT_REFRESH_TTL,
default 0: never expires) are HS256 JWTs; send the access token as Authorization: Bearer <token>
post.summary: creates a user and returns their tokens

post.description:
- creates the child profile and links it to the caller in the same transaction;
the caller is the child's first parent
- any signed-in role (user, paid_user, admin) may add children
- name is required, at most 100 characters; age is required, 0..18; gender is male or female
- photo_id is an optional id from POST /v1/media (422 if unknown)
post.summary: adds a child to the signed-in user

get.description: - only the child's parents can read it; any other id, or a deleted child, is 404
get.summary: one of the signed-in user's children
lists a child's completions, newest first

post.description:
- only the child's parents can record (404 otherwise); the activity must be published (404)
- the day is the current date in Uzbekistan (UTC+5); repeating the same activity on the same
day returns the existing completion, replacing its note if a new one is sent
- note is the caregiver's optional reflection, at most 1000 characters (422)
post.summary: marks an activity done for a child today

get.description:
- only the child's parents can ask (404 otherwise); the child's age is clamped to 2..6
- goal and minutes narrow the choice; minutes keeps activities with duration_minutes <= minutes
- activities the child has never done come first, then the one done longest ago;
ties are broken per child and per day, so the pick stays the same all day until it is done
- 404 when no published activity matches
get.summary: today's recommended activity for a child

get.description:
- current: consecutive days with a completion up to today, or up to yesterday while
today has none yet (the streak is not lost until a whole day is missed)
- longest: the longest such run; this_week: days with a completion since Monday
- days are counted in Uzbekistan time (UTC+5)
- the user row plus the current role (user, paid_user or admin)

delete.description:
- a soft delete: the user disappears from reads and their username and phone number can be used again
- their tokens are removed at once, so the access token used here stops working
- their children go too, unless another parent still has the child

patch.description:
- only the fields present in the body change; omitted or null fields are kept
- "" clears name, username or photo_id; phone_number cannot be cleared
- name: at most 100 characters; username: 3 to 32 of a-z, 0-9, '_' or '.' (lowercased);
photo_id: an id from POST /v1/media (422 if unknown)
- a new phone_number must be an Uzbek number (+998 and 9 digits) verified first:
POST /v1/otp/send and /v1/otp/verify with purpose update_user for the new number (403 otherwise);
the change uses the verification up. Sending the current number is not a change
- username or phone number already used by someone else: 409
patch.summary: edits the signed-in user's profile partially

get.description:
- only children linked to the caller; deleted children are left out
- GET /v1/children/{id} returns one of them
get.summary: lists the signed-in user's children, newest first

put.description:
- first POST /v1/otp/send and /v1/otp/verify with purpose reset_password for the
user's own phone number; without that verification: 403. A successful reset uses it up
- password: 8 to 72 bytes, stored as a bcrypt hash (422)
- returns a new token pair; every token issued before, on any device, stops working
put.summary: sets a new password for the signed-in user, confirmed by an SMS code

post.description:
- send form data (multipart/form-data or application/x-www-form-urlencoded) with one field "file":
either the file itself (multipart file part) or the file as a base64 string; a data URL
prefix such as "data:image/png;base64," is allowed
- accepted: JPEG, PNG or WebP, detected from the bytes, not from the file name (422 otherwise)
- at most MEDIA_MAX_SIZE bytes after decoding, default 5 MiB (422 otherwise)
- the answer's id goes into users.photo_id (PATCH /v1/admin/users/{id} {"photo_id": id});
url is where clients load the image from
- 503 when S3 is not configured (S3_BUCKET empty)
post.summary: uploads an image (a profile photo) to S3

parameters.description: the image: a file part, or a base64 string in the same field
parameters.name: file

post.description:
- phone_number: an Uzbek mobile number in E.164, +998 and 9 digits (422 otherwise)
- purpose: sign_up (the number must not belong to a user, 409 otherwise), update_user, or
reset_password (the number must belong to a user, 404 otherwise; used by forgot password and
PUT /v1/me/password)
- ip_address: the end user's IPv4 or IPv6 address, used for rate limits
- the code has 6 digits and is sent through Play Mobile; only its hash is stored
- the code is kept in Redis for expires_in seconds (OTP_TTL, default 2 minutes); a new
code replaces the previous one for the same phone and purpose
- rate limiter (429): one code per phone and purpose per resend_in seconds, and per hour
at most OTP_MAX_PER_PHONE_HOUR codes per phone and OTP_MAX_PER_IP_HOUR per IP
post.summary: sends a one-time code by SMS

parameters.description: where and why to send the code
parameters.name: body

post.description:
- phone_number and purpose must be the ones the code was sent for; code is 6 digits (422)
- a matching code is deleted, so it works only once; data is null
- wrong code: 422 with the attempts left; after OTP_MAX_VERIFY_ATTEMPTS wrong codes the
code is deleted and the answer is 429
- no code (never sent, expired after 2 minutes, or already used): 404
- OTP_DEFAULT_CODE, when configured (never in production), is accepted for any phone
and purpose without checking

error_note.example: limit must be a positive integer
phone number is not verified, verify a sign_up code with /v1/otp/verify first
a code was sent recently, request a new one in 42 seconds

expires_in.description: seconds until the access token expires

resend_in.description: seconds until a new code may be requested

expires_in.description: seconds until the access token expires
